title: We Let Our Financial Planners Write the Agents — Matthew Ragone, Range
talk_summary: A non-engineer financial planner describes how Range's domain experts write and maintain agent 'skills'—firm-specific procedures with required questions and hard limits—then test them on real cases and assign an owner and independent reviewer. The talk is a lightweight operating model for scaling agent workflows, not a technical or cost-efficiency benchmark.

takeaways.what_they_do: They package a workflow as a skill that includes mandatory preflight questions and explicit boundaries on what the agent must never do alone, not just step-by-step instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: What should it confirm with me instead of simply guessing? And the limits it must respect.
takeaways.numbers: 24 skills across company; 17 in planning after six months

takeaways.what_they_do: They run a new skill 5-10 times on real historical cases, fix edge cases, missing questions, and confident errors, then repeat before exposing it to the team.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run it five or 10 times on real cases before anyone else sees it.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every shipped skill has an owner to keep it current and a reviewer other than the author to check it before the team relies on it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The reviewer checks it before the team relies on it. And it's someone other than the author.

takeaways.technique: Start with repeated, judgeable, manual-heavy workflows
takeaways.what_they_do: They choose frequent workflows where good output is easy to judge quickly, rather than the flashiest or most complex work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You do it often and you know how to judge it.

takeaways.technique: Capture tacit judgment via narrated real cases
takeaways.what_they_do: They walk through real cases and narrate why each step is taken, what is looked for, and when to stop and ask, then encode that judgment into the skill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: why you're opening it, what you're looking for, what would make you stop and ask a question.
